source_notes: 70 CMS-mandated shoppable services plus 30 high-search-volume draft additions. The CMS 70 are predetermined by the federal Hospital Price Transparency Rule appendix; draft additions are flagged source='draft_addition' and should be refined against actual keyword volume data (Google Keyword Planner, Ahrefs) before locking. All descriptions written from scratch; no AMA CPT descriptor text reproduced. CPT codes should be verified against the current code set before going live, particularly for additions where coding has been updated in recent CPT revisions.

procedures.name: Office visit, established patient (level 3)
procedures.description: A standard follow-up office visit with a doctor you've seen before, typically lasting 20 to 29 minutes. Covers evaluation of a low-to-moderate complexity issue, like managing an ongoing condition or following up on test results. The most commonly billed office visit code in the United States.

procedures.name: Office visit, new patient (level 3)
procedures.description: An initial office visit with a doctor you haven't seen before, typically lasting 30 to 44 minutes. Includes a full history, examination, and an initial treatment plan for a low-to-moderate complexity issue.

procedures.name: Emergency room visit (level 3)
procedures.description: A moderate-complexity emergency department visit, the most common ER billing level. Typically covers conditions like sprains, mild infections, abdominal pain, or moderate injuries that need same-day evaluation but not hospitalization.

procedures.name: Initial hospital admission (level 1)
procedures.description: The first day of care after being admitted to the hospital, covering the admitting physician's evaluation, history, examination, and initial treatment plan. Billed once per admission.

procedures.name: Critical care, first hour
procedures.description: Care of a critically ill patient requiring constant physician attention for the first 30 to 74 minutes. Typically billed in intensive care units or for life-threatening emergencies.

procedures.name: Complete blood count (CBC) with differential
procedures.description: A standard blood test that measures red and white blood cells, platelets, hemoglobin, and the proportions of different white blood cell types. Used for routine checkups, infection screening, and monitoring of many conditions.

procedures.name: Comprehensive metabolic panel
procedures.description: A blood test measuring 14 substances including glucose, calcium, sodium, potassium, kidney function markers, and liver enzymes. Provides a broad snapshot of metabolic health and is routinely ordered for annual physicals or chronic disease monitoring.

procedures.name: Basic metabolic panel
procedures.description: A blood test measuring eight substances including glucose, calcium, sodium, potassium, and kidney function. A shorter version of the comprehensive metabolic panel, often ordered when liver function tests aren't needed.

procedures.name: Lipid panel (cholesterol test)
procedures.description: A blood test measuring cholesterol levels, including total cholesterol, HDL (good cholesterol), LDL (bad cholesterol), and triglycerides. Used to assess heart disease risk.

procedures.name: Hemoglobin A1c (diabetes test)
procedures.description: A blood test that measures average blood sugar levels over the past two to three months. Used to diagnose diabetes and monitor blood sugar control in people who have diabetes.

procedures.name: TSH thyroid function test
procedures.description: A blood test measuring thyroid-stimulating hormone, the most common screening test for thyroid problems. Used to diagnose hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism.

procedures.name: Urinalysis with microscopy
procedures.description: A laboratory analysis of a urine sample examining its chemical and microscopic properties. Used to detect urinary tract infections, kidney disease, diabetes, and other conditions.

procedures.name: PSA prostate cancer screening
procedures.description: A blood test measuring prostate-specific antigen levels, used to screen for prostate cancer and monitor men who have been diagnosed with prostate conditions. Generally recommended starting at age 50 for average-risk men.

procedures.name: HIV antibody test
procedures.description: A blood test screening for antibodies to HIV. Routinely recommended for adults aged 15 to 65 at least once, and more frequently for those at higher risk.

procedures.name: Vitamin D blood test
procedures.description: A blood test measuring vitamin D levels, used to diagnose deficiency, monitor treatment, or evaluate bone health and certain chronic conditions.

procedures.name: MRI brain without contrast
procedures.description: Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain using strong magnets and radio waves to create detailed images, performed without contrast dye. Used to evaluate headaches, suspected strokes, tumors, multiple sclerosis, and other neurological conditions.

procedures.name: MRI brain with contrast
procedures.description: Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain performed with an injected contrast dye that highlights blood vessels and certain tissue abnormalities. Often used when evaluating tumors, infections, or vascular problems.

procedures.name: MRI brain with and without contrast
procedures.description: Magnetic resonance imaging of the brain performed both before and after injecting contrast dye, producing the most complete picture of brain structures. Common for tumor evaluation, multiple sclerosis monitoring, and complex neurological cases.

procedures.name: MRI lower back (lumbar spine) without contrast
procedures.description: Magnetic resonance imaging of the lower back, performed without contrast dye. The most common imaging test ordered for persistent low back pain, suspected herniated discs, or sciatica.

procedures.name: MRI knee without contrast
procedures.description: Magnetic resonance imaging of the knee, performed without contrast dye. Commonly ordered to evaluate knee pain, suspected meniscus or ligament tears, and unexplained swelling. Typically takes 30 to 45 minutes.

procedures.name: CT head without contrast
procedures.description: A computed tomography scan of the head using X-rays to create cross-sectional images of the brain and skull. Commonly performed in emergency settings to evaluate head injuries, suspected stroke, or sudden severe headaches.

procedures.name: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
procedures.description: A computed tomography scan of the abdomen and pelvis performed with contrast dye, producing detailed cross-sectional images of internal organs. Commonly ordered for abdominal pain evaluation, kidney stones, suspected appendicitis, or cancer staging.

procedures.name: CT chest without contrast
procedures.description: A computed tomography scan of the chest performed without contrast dye, producing detailed images of the lungs, heart, and other structures. Used to evaluate persistent cough, chest pain, lung nodules, and suspected pneumonia.

procedures.name: Screening mammogram
procedures.description: A low-dose X-ray of both breasts used to screen for breast cancer in women without symptoms. Generally recommended annually or every two years starting between ages 40 and 50.

procedures.name: Diagnostic mammogram (both breasts)
procedures.description: A more detailed mammogram performed when there's a specific concern, such as a lump, breast pain, or follow-up to an abnormal screening mammogram. Includes additional views beyond the standard screening protocol.

procedures.name: DEXA bone density scan
procedures.description: A low-dose X-ray that measures bone mineral density, used to screen for osteoporosis and assess fracture risk. Typically recommended for women starting at age 65 and men with risk factors.

procedures.name: Chest X-ray (2 views)
procedures.description: A standard imaging test using X-rays to produce a picture of the chest, including the heart, lungs, ribs, and diaphragm. The most commonly ordered imaging study, used to evaluate cough, shortness of breath, chest pain, and many other conditions.

procedures.name: Complete abdominal ultrasound
procedures.description: An ultrasound examination of the entire abdomen, including the liver, gallbladder, pancreas, spleen, kidneys, and major blood vessels. Used to evaluate abdominal pain, suspected gallstones, and abnormal liver enzymes.

procedures.name: Pregnancy ultrasound (second or third trimester)
procedures.description: An ultrasound examination during the second or third trimester of pregnancy to assess fetal anatomy, growth, position, and the placenta. Includes evaluation of amniotic fluid and uterine structures.

procedures.name: Echocardiogram (complete with Doppler)
procedures.description: An ultrasound of the heart that produces detailed images of heart structures and measures blood flow through the chambers and valves. Used to evaluate heart murmurs, chest pain, shortness of breath, and known heart conditions.

procedures.name: EKG (electrocardiogram, 12-lead)
procedures.description: A quick test that records the heart's electrical activity using 12 electrodes placed on the chest, arms, and legs. Used to evaluate chest pain, palpitations, and screen for heart conditions.

procedures.name: Holter monitor (24-48 hour heart monitor)
procedures.description: A portable device worn for 24 to 48 hours that continuously records heart rhythm. Used to detect irregular heartbeats that may not appear during a standard EKG.

procedures.name: Cardiac stress test (treadmill)
procedures.description: A test that measures heart function while exercising on a treadmill or stationary bike, including continuous EKG monitoring and blood pressure measurement. Used to evaluate chest pain, suspected coronary artery disease, and exercise capacity.

procedures.name: Hemodialysis treatment
procedures.description: A treatment that filters waste and excess fluid from the blood for patients with kidney failure. Typically performed three times per week, each session lasting three to four hours.

procedures.name: Diagnostic colonoscopy
procedures.description: An examination of the large intestine using a flexible camera inserted through the rectum. Used for colorectal cancer screening starting at age 45 and to evaluate symptoms like rectal bleeding or persistent changes in bowel habits.

procedures.name: Colonoscopy with biopsy
procedures.description: A colonoscopy during which one or more tissue samples are taken for laboratory analysis. Typically billed when polyps or suspicious areas are found and sampled during the procedure.

procedures.name: Upper GI endoscopy (EGD)
procedures.description: An examination of the esophagus, stomach, and beginning of the small intestine using a flexible camera passed through the mouth. Used to evaluate persistent heartburn, swallowing difficulty, abdominal pain, and suspected ulcers.

procedures.name: Allergy skin testing
procedures.description: A series of skin tests in which small amounts of suspected allergens are applied to the skin to identify allergic reactions. Each test is billed per allergen tested, with most panels including 30 to 70 tests.

procedures.name: Spirometry (breathing test)
procedures.description: A breathing test that measures how much air a person can inhale and exhale, and how quickly. Used to diagnose and monitor asthma, COPD, and other lung conditions.

procedures.name: Pulmonary function test with bronchodilator
procedures.description: A more comprehensive breathing test that includes spirometry both before and after a medication that opens airways. Used to confirm asthma diagnosis and assess bronchodilator response.

procedures.name: Cataract surgery with lens implant
procedures.description: An outpatient eye surgery that removes the clouded natural lens and replaces it with a clear artificial lens. The most commonly performed surgery in the United States, typically takes 15 to 30 minutes per eye.

procedures.name: Tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy (under age 12)
procedures.description: Surgical removal of the tonsils and adenoids in a patient under age 12. Commonly performed for recurrent throat infections, obstructive sleep apnea, or chronic sleep-disordered breathing in children.

procedures.name: Tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy (age 12 and over)
procedures.description: Surgical removal of the tonsils and adenoids in a patient age 12 or older. Adult recovery is typically longer and more painful than the pediatric procedure.

procedures.name: Inguinal hernia repair (open)
procedures.description: Surgical repair of a hernia in the groin through an open incision, typically with mesh reinforcement. One of the most common general surgery procedures.

procedures.name: Laparoscopic gallbladder removal
procedures.description: Removal of the gallbladder through small incisions using a camera and specialized instruments. Most commonly performed for symptomatic gallstones; recovery is typically faster than open surgery.

procedures.name: Laparoscopic appendectomy
procedures.description: Removal of the appendix through small incisions using a camera and specialized instruments, typically performed for acute appendicitis. Recovery is usually faster than open surgery.

procedures.name: Abdominal hysterectomy
procedures.description: Surgical removal of the uterus through an incision in the abdomen, sometimes including removal of fallopian tubes and ovaries. Performed for fibroids, endometriosis, abnormal bleeding, or gynecologic cancers.

procedures.name: Vaginal hysterectomy
procedures.description: Surgical removal of the uterus through the vagina, leaving no abdominal scar. Typically results in shorter hospital stay and faster recovery than abdominal hysterectomy when feasible.

procedures.name: Total knee replacement
procedures.description: Surgical replacement of a damaged knee joint with an artificial implant. One of the most common major orthopedic surgeries in the United States, typically performed for severe osteoarthritis.

procedures.name: Total hip replacement
procedures.description: Surgical replacement of a damaged hip joint with an artificial implant. Commonly performed for severe osteoarthritis, hip fractures, and avascular necrosis.

procedures.name: Carpal tunnel release surgery
procedures.description: Surgical release of the transverse carpal ligament to relieve pressure on the median nerve, treating carpal tunnel syndrome. Performed as an outpatient procedure under local or regional anesthesia.

procedures.name: Lumbar spinal fusion (posterior)
procedures.description: Surgery that permanently joins two or more vertebrae in the lower back using bone graft and often metal hardware. Performed for severe back pain, spinal instability, deformity, or after disc removal.

procedures.name: Cervical spinal fusion (anterior)
procedures.description: Surgery that joins two or more vertebrae in the neck through an incision in the front of the throat, typically including removal of a damaged disc. Performed for severe neck pain, herniated discs, and cervical spondylosis.

procedures.name: Bunion correction surgery
procedures.description: Surgical correction of a bunion (bony bump at the base of the big toe) involving cutting and realigning the first metatarsal bone. Performed for painful bunions that limit walking or shoe wear.

procedures.name: Rotator cuff repair (arthroscopic)
procedures.description: Minimally invasive surgical repair of a torn rotator cuff in the shoulder, performed through small incisions using a camera. Commonly performed for full-thickness rotator cuff tears that have failed conservative treatment.

procedures.name: Lumbar epidural steroid injection
procedures.description: An injection of steroid medication into the epidural space of the lower spine to reduce inflammation and treat back or leg pain. Commonly performed for sciatica, herniated discs, and spinal stenosis.

procedures.name: TURP (transurethral prostate resection)
procedures.description: A surgical procedure that removes part of the prostate through the urethra to relieve urinary symptoms caused by an enlarged prostate. Typically performed under spinal or general anesthesia.

procedures.name: Vasectomy
procedures.description: A surgical procedure for male sterilization that cuts and seals the vas deferens. Typically performed as an outpatient procedure under local anesthesia in 15 to 30 minutes.

procedures.name: Laparoscopic tubal ligation
procedures.description: A surgical procedure for female sterilization that closes the fallopian tubes, performed through small abdominal incisions. Commonly known as having your tubes tied.

procedures.name: Lumpectomy (partial mastectomy)
procedures.description: Surgical removal of a breast tumor along with a small margin of surrounding healthy tissue, preserving most of the breast. The standard initial surgery for many early-stage breast cancers.

procedures.name: Total mastectomy
procedures.description: Surgical removal of an entire breast, performed for breast cancer treatment or risk reduction in high-risk patients. Often performed with sentinel lymph node biopsy and may include reconstruction planning.

procedures.name: Septoplasty (deviated septum repair)
procedures.description: Surgical correction of a crooked nasal septum to improve breathing through the nose. Typically performed as an outpatient procedure with recovery in one to two weeks.

procedures.name: Umbilical hernia repair
procedures.description: Surgical repair of a hernia at or near the belly button. Common in adults after pregnancy or significant weight changes; usually performed as an outpatient procedure with mesh.

procedures.name: Ear tube placement (tympanostomy)
procedures.description: A surgical procedure that inserts small tubes into the eardrums to drain fluid and prevent ear infections. The most common reason for general anesthesia in children, typically performed for recurrent ear infections or persistent fluid behind the eardrum.

procedures.name: Skin lesion removal (benign, up to 0.5 cm)
procedures.description: Excision of a benign skin growth such as a mole or cyst, including a small margin of surrounding skin. Typically performed under local anesthesia in a doctor's office or outpatient setting.

procedures.name: Vaginal delivery (global package)
procedures.description: A comprehensive maternity package covering routine prenatal care, vaginal delivery, and postpartum care for low-risk pregnancies. Hospital facility fees are typically billed separately from the physician's global fee.

procedures.name: Cesarean delivery (global package)
procedures.description: A comprehensive maternity package covering routine prenatal care, cesarean delivery, and postpartum care. Hospital facility fees are typically billed separately and are higher than vaginal delivery.

procedures.name: Vaginal birth after cesarean (VBAC) global package
procedures.description: A comprehensive maternity package covering prenatal care, vaginal delivery after a previous cesarean, and postpartum care. Requires specific clinical eligibility and not all hospitals offer VBAC services.

procedures.name: Anesthesia for screening colonoscopy
procedures.description: Anesthesia services provided during a colonoscopy, typically billed separately from the colonoscopy itself. Usually involves moderate sedation or monitored anesthesia care administered by an anesthesiologist or CRNA.

procedures.name: Anesthesia for upper endoscopy
procedures.description: Anesthesia services provided during an upper GI endoscopy, billed separately from the endoscopy itself. Typically moderate sedation or monitored anesthesia care.

procedures.name: PET/CT scan, whole body
procedures.description: A combined positron emission tomography and CT scan that uses a radioactive tracer to detect cancer activity and metabolic activity throughout the body. Used for cancer staging, treatment monitoring, and recurrence detection.

procedures.name: MRI cervical spine (neck) without contrast
procedures.description: Magnetic resonance imaging of the neck portion of the spine, performed without contrast dye. Commonly ordered for persistent neck pain, suspected disc problems, and unexplained arm pain or numbness.

procedures.name: MRI thoracic spine (mid-back) without contrast
procedures.description: Magnetic resonance imaging of the middle portion of the spine, performed without contrast dye. Used to evaluate mid-back pain and certain neurological symptoms.

procedures.name: MRI abdomen with and without contrast
procedures.description: Magnetic resonance imaging of the abdomen performed both before and after injecting contrast dye, producing the most detailed view of abdominal organs. Used for liver lesion characterization, pancreatic evaluation, and other complex abdominal questions.

procedures.name: CT cardiac calcium scoring
procedures.description: A specialized CT scan that measures calcified plaque in the coronary arteries to assess heart disease risk. Increasingly used as a preventive screening for adults at intermediate cardiac risk.

procedures.name: Nuclear cardiac stress test
procedures.description: A cardiac stress test that uses a small amount of radioactive tracer and imaging to evaluate blood flow to the heart during rest and stress. Used when standard treadmill stress tests are inconclusive or not possible.

procedures.name: Sleep study (in-lab polysomnography)
procedures.description: An overnight test in a sleep lab that records brain activity, breathing, heart rate, oxygen levels, and movements during sleep. Used to diagnose sleep apnea, narcolepsy, and other sleep disorders.

procedures.name: ACL reconstruction (arthroscopic)
procedures.description: Surgical reconstruction of a torn anterior cruciate ligament in the knee using a tendon graft, performed through small incisions with arthroscopic guidance. Commonly performed for athletes and active individuals after ACL tears.

procedures.name: Knee arthroscopy with meniscectomy
procedures.description: Minimally invasive knee surgery that removes the torn portion of a meniscus through small incisions using a camera. The most common surgical treatment for a torn meniscus; meniscus repair (a separate procedure) is performed only when the tear is in a region that can heal.

procedures.name: Sinus surgery (endoscopic, with tissue removal)
procedures.description: Endoscopic sinus surgery that opens blocked sinus passages and removes diseased tissue. Performed for chronic sinusitis that hasn't responded to medical treatment, nasal polyps, or recurrent sinus infections.

procedures.name: Pacemaker insertion (dual chamber)
procedures.description: Surgical implantation of a dual-chamber pacemaker to regulate heart rhythm, with leads placed in both the right atrium and right ventricle. Performed for various heart rhythm disorders including bradycardia and heart block.

procedures.name: Cardiac catheterization (left heart)
procedures.description: A diagnostic procedure that uses contrast dye and X-ray imaging to visualize the heart's blood vessels and chambers. Used to evaluate chest pain, suspected coronary artery disease, and abnormal stress test results.

procedures.name: Coronary angioplasty with stent
procedures.description: A minimally invasive procedure that opens a blocked coronary artery using a balloon and inserts a stent to keep the artery open. Performed for significant coronary artery blockages causing symptoms or after a heart attack.

procedures.name: Newborn circumcision
procedures.description: Surgical removal of the foreskin from a newborn male infant, typically performed within the first few days of life. Performed for religious, cultural, or medical reasons.

procedures.name: Chemotherapy infusion (first hour)
procedures.description: Intravenous administration of chemotherapy medication for the first hour of treatment. Each additional hour and each additional drug are billed separately. Hospital facility fees and drug costs are typically billed separately and dominate the total cost.

procedures.name: Intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) treatment
procedures.description: A single session of intensity-modulated radiation therapy that delivers precise radiation doses to a tumor while sparing surrounding tissue. Typically administered in 20 to 40 daily sessions over several weeks.

procedures.name: IUD insertion
procedures.description: Placement of an intrauterine device for long-acting contraception. Typically performed in a doctor's office in 15 to 30 minutes; the device itself is billed separately.

procedures.name: IUD removal
procedures.description: Removal of an intrauterine device, typically performed in a doctor's office in a few minutes. Required at the end of the device's effective lifespan or when the patient chooses to discontinue use.

procedures.name: Skin biopsy (tangential)
procedures.description: A minor surgical procedure that removes a sample of skin for laboratory analysis, typically to evaluate suspicious moles or skin lesions for cancer or other conditions.

procedures.name: Breast biopsy (ultrasound-guided)
procedures.description: A minimally invasive biopsy of breast tissue performed under ultrasound guidance, typically using a needle. Used to evaluate suspicious findings from a mammogram or breast ultrasound.

procedures.name: Prostate biopsy
procedures.description: A procedure that removes small samples of prostate tissue for laboratory analysis, typically performed when PSA levels are elevated or a prostate exam is abnormal. Usually performed transrectally with ultrasound guidance.

procedures.name: Bone marrow biopsy
procedures.description: A procedure that removes a small core of bone marrow tissue, typically from the hip bone, for laboratory analysis. Used to diagnose blood disorders, certain cancers, and unexplained blood count abnormalities.

procedures.name: Lumbar puncture (spinal tap)
procedures.description: A procedure that collects cerebrospinal fluid from the lower back using a thin needle, used to diagnose meningitis, multiple sclerosis, and other neurological conditions. Typically performed in an outpatient or emergency setting.

procedures.name: Initial psychiatric diagnostic evaluation
procedures.description: An initial psychiatric or mental health assessment, including history, mental status examination, and diagnostic formulation. Typically performed by a psychiatrist, psychologist, or licensed clinical therapist.

procedures.name: Initial psychiatric evaluation with medication management
procedures.description: An initial psychiatric evaluation conducted by a physician that includes prescribing authority and medication consideration. Distinguished from the standard psychiatric evaluation by the inclusion of medical services.

procedures.name: Individual therapy session (45 minutes)
procedures.description: A 38-to-52-minute psychotherapy session with a licensed mental health provider. The most commonly billed therapy code for outpatient mental health treatment.

procedures.name: Group therapy session
procedures.description: A group psychotherapy session led by a licensed mental health provider, typically with three to twelve participants. Used for substance use treatment, anxiety, depression, and various other mental health conditions.

procedures.name: Home sleep study
procedures.description: An unattended sleep study performed at home using portable monitoring equipment that records breathing, oxygen, and heart rate during sleep. Used to diagnose obstructive sleep apnea in patients without significant other medical conditions.

procedures.name: Spinal cord stimulator trial
procedures.description: A temporary placement of electrodes near the spinal cord to test whether spinal cord stimulation will relieve chronic pain. Typically followed by permanent implantation if successful.

procedures.name: Cardiac ablation for atrial fibrillation
procedures.description: A catheter-based procedure that uses radiofrequency energy or freezing to destroy areas of heart tissue causing atrial fibrillation. Performed to restore normal heart rhythm in patients with persistent or recurrent AFib.

procedures.name: Cesarean section (with complications)
procedures.description: A C-section delivery where the mother or baby had additional complications or conditions during the stay. One of the most common reasons for a hospital admission.

procedures.name: Cesarean section (without complications)
procedures.description: A standard C-section delivery without major additional complications.

procedures.name: Vaginal delivery (with complications)
procedures.description: A vaginal childbirth admission where complicating diagnoses were present.

procedures.name: Vaginal delivery (without complications)
procedures.description: A routine vaginal childbirth hospital stay without complicating diagnoses — the most common delivery type. Reflects the full inpatient stay, not just the delivery service.

procedures.name: Hip or knee replacement (without major complications)
procedures.description: Major joint replacement of the hip or knee without major complications — among the most common and most shopped inpatient surgeries.

procedures.name: Hip or knee replacement (with major complications)
procedures.description: Major hip or knee joint replacement where major complications or conditions were present.

procedures.name: Hip and femur procedures (with major complications)
procedures.description: Surgical repair of the hip or thigh bone (other than joint replacement), such as fixing a fracture, with major complications.

procedures.name: Hip and femur procedures (with complications)
procedures.description: Surgical repair of the hip or thigh bone (other than joint replacement) with complications.

procedures.name: Hip and femur procedures (without complications)
procedures.description: Surgical repair of the hip or thigh bone (other than joint replacement) without major complications.

procedures.name: Spinal fusion, except cervical (without major complications)
procedures.description: Surgery to permanently join two or more vertebrae in the back, excluding the neck, without major complications.

procedures.name: Coronary stent (drug-eluting, without major complications)
procedures.description: A hospital stay to open a blocked heart artery and place a medication-coated stent, without major complications. Reflects the full inpatient admission.

procedures.name: Heart attack, discharged alive (with major complications)
procedures.description: Hospital care for an acute heart attack (myocardial infarction) with major complications, where the patient survived to discharge.

procedures.name: Heart attack, discharged alive (with complications)
procedures.description: Hospital care for an acute heart attack with complications, discharged alive.

procedures.name: Heart attack, discharged alive (without complications)
procedures.description: Hospital care for an acute heart attack without major complications, discharged alive.

procedures.name: Heart failure and shock (with major complications)
procedures.description: Hospital admission for heart failure with major complications — one of the most frequent inpatient diagnoses.

procedures.name: Heart failure and shock (with complications)
procedures.description: Hospital admission for heart failure with complications.

procedures.name: Heart failure and shock (without complications)
procedures.description: Hospital admission for heart failure without major complications.

procedures.name: Cardiac arrhythmia (with major complications)
procedures.description: Hospital care for an irregular heartbeat or conduction disorder with major complications.

procedures.name: Cardiac arrhythmia (with complications)
procedures.description: Hospital care for an irregular heartbeat or conduction disorder with complications.

procedures.name: Cardiac arrhythmia (without complications)
procedures.description: Hospital care for an irregular heartbeat or conduction disorder without major complications.

procedures.name: Stroke (with major complications)
procedures.description: Hospital care for an intracranial hemorrhage or cerebral infarction (stroke) with major complications.

procedures.name: Stroke (with complications)
procedures.description: Hospital care for a stroke (intracranial hemorrhage or cerebral infarction) with complications.

procedures.name: Stroke (without complications)
procedures.description: Hospital care for a stroke (intracranial hemorrhage or cerebral infarction) without major complications.

procedures.name: Pulmonary edema and respiratory failure
procedures.description: Hospital care for fluid in the lungs or failure of the lungs to oxygenate the blood adequately.

procedures.name: COPD (with major complications)
procedures.description: Hospital admission for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) with major complications.

procedures.name: COPD (with complications)
procedures.description: Hospital admission for COPD with complications.

procedures.name: COPD (without complications)
procedures.description: Hospital admission for COPD without major complications.

procedures.name: Pneumonia and pleurisy (with major complications)
procedures.description: Hospital care for simple pneumonia or pleurisy with major complications.

procedures.name: Pneumonia and pleurisy (with complications)
procedures.description: Hospital care for simple pneumonia or pleurisy with complications.

procedures.name: Pneumonia and pleurisy (without complications)
procedures.description: Hospital care for simple pneumonia or pleurisy without major complications.

procedures.name: Sepsis (with major complications)
procedures.description: Hospital care for septicemia or severe sepsis (a life-threatening response to infection) with major complications, without prolonged ventilation.

procedures.name: Sepsis (without major complications)
procedures.description: Hospital care for septicemia or severe sepsis without major complications or prolonged ventilation.

procedures.name: Major bowel procedure (with major complications)
procedures.description: Major surgery on the small or large intestine with major complications.

procedures.name: Major bowel procedure (with complications)
procedures.description: Major surgery on the small or large intestine with complications.

procedures.name: Major bowel procedure (without complications)
procedures.description: Major surgery on the small or large intestine without major complications.

procedures.name: GI hemorrhage (with major complications)
procedures.description: Hospital care for gastrointestinal bleeding with major complications.

procedures.name: GI hemorrhage (with complications)
procedures.description: Hospital care for gastrointestinal bleeding with complications.

procedures.name: GI hemorrhage (without complications)
procedures.description: Hospital care for gastrointestinal bleeding without major complications.

procedures.name: Digestive disorders, e.g. gastroenteritis (with major complications)
procedures.description: Hospital care for esophagitis, gastroenteritis, or other digestive disorders with major complications.

procedures.name: Digestive disorders, e.g. gastroenteritis (without major complications)
procedures.description: Hospital care for esophagitis, gastroenteritis, or other digestive disorders without major complications.

procedures.name: Laparoscopic gallbladder removal (with major complications)
procedures.description: Minimally invasive (keyhole) surgery to remove the gallbladder, with major complications.

procedures.name: Laparoscopic gallbladder removal (with complications)
procedures.description: Minimally invasive surgery to remove the gallbladder, with complications.

procedures.name: Laparoscopic gallbladder removal (without complications)
procedures.description: Minimally invasive (keyhole) surgery to remove the gallbladder without major complications.

procedures.name: Kidney failure (with major complications)
procedures.description: Hospital care for renal (kidney) failure with major complications.

procedures.name: Kidney failure (with complications)
procedures.description: Hospital care for renal failure with complications.

procedures.name: Kidney failure (without complications)
procedures.description: Hospital care for renal failure without major complications.

procedures.name: Kidney or urinary tract infection (with major complications)
procedures.description: Hospital care for a kidney or urinary tract infection with major complications.

procedures.name: Kidney or urinary tract infection (without major complications)
procedures.description: Hospital care for a kidney or urinary tract infection without major complications.

procedures.name: Diabetes (with major complications)
procedures.description: Hospital admission for diabetes with major complications.

procedures.name: Diabetes (with complications)
procedures.description: Hospital admission for diabetes with complications.

procedures.name: Diabetes (without complications)
procedures.description: Hospital admission for diabetes without major complications.

procedures.name: Cellulitis (with major complications)
procedures.description: Hospital care for cellulitis (a bacterial skin infection) with major complications.

procedures.name: Cellulitis (without major complications)
